title: Should the RC confirmation format change now?
subtitle: A concise approval brief separating live compatibility, future protocol work, and the unproven human-intent boundary.

audience.role: Owner approving the protocol alignment PR
audience.participationGoal: Approve, condition, or reject the RC alignment without risking today's connector

sourceScope.summary: Representative repository and plan evidence for the live compatibility lane, proposed RC serialization, and confirmation trust boundary.

sources.label: Authored capability registry
sources.evidence: Capabilities are authored once and projected into agent and portal surfaces.

sources.label: Server confirmation binding
sources.evidence: The server seals action, grant, expiry, and nonce, then verifies binding and single use during resolution.

sources.label: Client human-interaction boundary
sources.evidence: The client renders confirmation outside model-controlled content, accepts the human interaction, and does not expose the resolution control to model tool calls.

sources.label: RC alignment plan
sources.evidence: The plan proposes a separate RC serializer and byte-pinned compatibility fixtures.

sources.label: Ratified protocol shape
sources.evidence: The standard defines result-level state and keyed request and response maps for the upcoming protocol lane.

visuals.title: Where human intent enters
visuals.teachingGoal: Separate model request, client rendering, human interaction, and server verification.

items.label: Model requests action
items.detail: The model can propose a sensitive operation but cannot directly use the client confirmation control.

items.label: Server parks and seals
items.detail: The server binds the exact proposal, grant, expiry, and nonce into the request state.

items.label: Client renders boundary
items.detail: The client presents the prompt outside model-controlled content and waits for user interaction.

items.label: Server verifies and resolves
items.detail: The server checks integrity, binding, expiry, replay status, and the returned decision.

visuals.title: Compatibility and RC are separate decisions
visuals.teachingGoal: Show why only the version-specific serializer should diverge.

items.label: Compat lane
items.detail: Today's connector keeps its current message bytes and behavior, pinned by fixtures.

items.label: RC lane
items.detail: The future lane adopts the ratified result and request-map shapes before released clients depend on it.

decisionBrief.question: Should the PR change the RC wire format while freezing today's compatibility output?
decisionBrief.recommendation: Approve with two conditions: exact SEP conformance on RC and byte-for-byte compatibility fixtures for the live lane.

rationale.title: The duplication belongs at the serialization boundary
rationale.body: Separating version-specific message construction protects released clients without duplicating capability policy or execution logic.

currentState.title: One registry feeds both surfaces
currentState.body: Agent tools and portal controls derive from one authored capability source.

currentState.title: The live lane already serves released clients
currentState.body: Changing shared message builders would risk altering today's connector responses.

proposedChange.title: Fork only the serializers
proposedChange.body: Compatibility retains frozen builders while RC receives standard-shaped result and request maps.

proposedChange.title: Leave business behavior shared
proposedChange.body: Capability definitions, parking, policy, and resolution remain common beneath the protocol-specific wire layer.

approvalCriteria.criterion: RC output matches the ratified protocol
approvalCriteria.evidenceRequired: Fixture assertions for result-level state, keyed requests and keyed responses.
Byte-level golden tests covering every live confirmation response.

approvalCriteria.criterion: Human intent has an explicit boundary
approvalCriteria.evidenceRequired: Client tests prove confirmation renders outside model control and resolution is unavailable as a model-callable action.

risks.risk: Shared builder edits leak into compatibility
risks.impact: Released clients receive an unannounced wire-format change.
risks.mitigation: Keep policy shared but split serializer functions and pin compat bytes.

risks.risk: Token security is mistaken for proof of human intent
risks.impact: The design could overclaim that the model cannot approve.
risks.mitigation: Test the client interaction boundary independently from server token integrity.

openQuestions.question: What event retires the compatibility serializer?
openQuestions.whyItMatters: Temporary duplication becomes permanent unless the migration has an observable exit condition.

limitations: This synthetic fixture tests the artifact contract and renderer, not a live production checkout.
